audit_scope: Independent masked-output audit of the supplied 27 paired cases. Tool labels remain X and Y.
source_access_statement: These are the only task source files read. No browsing, memory, other source files, prior results, intended-error labels, or delegation were used. Inputs were not edited.
methodology: Read every case and every supplied finding. Judge the actual source language, not the case identifier or rule name.

Separate detecting a defect from supplying a faithful, grammatical replacement in the complete sentence. For sentences with two misspellings, a correct single-span repair may leave the other flagged misspelling; assess the combined top repairs separately.
Inspect the explicit top_replacement and every entry in all_replacements. Do not assume list order identifies the top replacement.
Treat legitimate terminology, passive constructions, meaningful repetition, contextual fragments, and attachment ambiguity as potentially correct. Do not invent intended meaning.
Use American English as supplied, while honoring the explicitly accepted custom spellings hypoxaemia and thermocouple.
Exclude diagnostics on code-masking whitespace from intrinsic prose errors. Do not count deliberately masked code misspellings as unflagged prose.

Spans are zero-based Unicode code-point offsets with an exclusive end. All 32 supplied diagnostic spans match their submitted substring under that convention, including the emoji cases. This does not by itself establish UTF-16 editor-integration behavior.
Comma-splice and tense judgments use the ordinary standalone factual/reporting reading and state the relevant rhetorical or narrative qualifications.
Counts describe only these cases; duplicated spelling examples, scope choices, a small nonrepresentative sample, and different diagnostic coverage prevent a general product ranking.

category_definitions.valid error detection: The flag locates a real source defect. This category does not guarantee that the suggested repair is correct.
category_definitions.optional style/dialect preference: The source is legitimate; the proposed change is an optional convention or dialect normalization. A declared accepted spelling can still make that raw flag unwanted under the task contract.
category_definitions.unwanted flag on legitimate text/termino: No language defect is established at the flagged text; the flag is unnecessary or the replacements misrepresent a legitimate construction or term.
category_definitions.input-masking artifact: The flag arises inside the spaces generated by masking fenced code, rather than from an intrinsic original-prose problem.
category_definitions.uncertain: Available context or terminology knowledge is insufficient for a reliable classification. No returned diagnostic required this primary label; contextual qualifications are recorded separately.
